title: A new agreement with room for warmth

captions.physics: Considering both people’s domestic needs fairly
captions.energy: Cutting former care away too sharply

meaning: Your domestic agreement supports renewal when leaving a demanding form does not remove simple available expressions of care.
text: You can arrange support through fair participation: discussing essentials, considering capacity and dividing actual work. Justice in the physical position of Muladhara describes these actions. Death in energy tests your footing through sharply rejecting the old, as though ending an inconvenient form must end the entire familiar way of caring. The Empress in emotions seeks acceptance, warmth and sufficiency. Even fair relief can feel cold if released time has no new living form and home seems allowed only to contain the absence of old duties rather than simple pleasure for two.

For example, you fairly decide to stop lengthy cooking. Brief meetings at the table disappear alongside complicated dishes although they required little work. **Simplifying care does not mean ending it entirely.** Tea and simple food preserve acceptance without restoring the old load. The agreement answers your actual capacity, and warmth need not choose between demanding routines and the complete absence of recognisable kindness.

The difficulty is treating every familiar detail as going backwards. The new rule is defended more strictly, making a pleasant gesture seem the dangerous beginning of former obligations. Home gains free time while losing warmth. Support grows through change that distinguishes a demanding form from its living meaning, letting care remain simple and manageable instead of only entirely cancelled. Renewal can then offer both relief and belonging.
